recentItems.title: The Surprising Beauty of Mosquitos | Felix Hol | TED
recentItems.description:
Most people hate mosquitoes, but biotechnologist and TED Fellow Felix Hol thinks they're beautiful. He takes us inside his lab, where his team developed some unusual ways to study how these blood-sucking insects find us and feed so fast. He also explains why insecticides may send certain mosquitoes into overdrive — and how we can find smarter ways to curb the diseases they spread. (Recorded at TED Fellows Films on April 15, 2026)

recentItems.title: The most teachable moments might happen when parents aren’t there #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Whether it’s micromanaging playtime, constantly hovering or incessantly texting, the adult takeover of childhood has created a crisis of anxiety in both children and parents, says Lenore Skenazy, cofounder and president of Let Grow, an organization dedicated to normalizing childhood independence. With wit and humor, she lays out the unexpected benefits of letting our kids be a bit more “free range” — and shows why the most teachable moments happen when parents aren’t there.

recentItems.title: How to Make Friends (and Keep Them) | Sheridan Voysey | TED
recentItems.description:
Who could you call at 2am when everything’s gone wrong? Friendship expert Sheridan Voysey believes we’re in a friendship recession, with many of us forgetting how to foster meaningful relationships. He explores three hidden barriers keeping us apart, why it feels harder to make friends as an adult — and how to nurture the deep connections that sustain us. (Recorded at TEDxSt Albans on October 15, 2025)

recentItems.description: Every rom-com tells us what romance is supposed to look like — but does seeking it only in relationships mean we’re missing it everywhere else? Check out the full episode of @cornerpiecepod, at https://link.mgln.ai/VBzPbb.

recentItems.title: Can You Spot the Lies in Your News Feed? | Laura Smythe | TED
recentItems.description:
Laura Smythe spent years in legacy newsrooms, and she thinks the habits journalists use to vet information should belong to all of us. Using Fyre Festival as a cautionary tale, she explains why media literacy is a vital skill in our age of deepfakes and algorithmic feeds — and describes the country that’s already found a way to start teaching it in elementary school. (Recorded at TED Democracy Philadelphia on June 13, 2026)

recentItems.title: The “Godfather of AI” on the Risks That Worry Him Most | Geoffrey Hinton | TED
recentItems.description:
Geoffrey Hinton helped create the neural networks behind today's AI, won a Nobel Prize for it — and has spent the years since warning about where it's headed. In conversation with journalist Nicholas Thompson, Hinton shares the AI risks he's worried about, sketches out a best-case future for the technology and explores whether or not chatbots have subjective experience. Plus: hear his thoughts on the one rule he'd give superintelligent AI. (Recorded at TEDAI Vienna 2026 on October 30, 2026)

recentItems.title: Could this potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments? #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: What if medicines could "speak" directly to your cells? Protein designer and TED Fellow Chris Bahl introduces a new generation of miniproteins: AI-designed medicines that can deliver detailed instructions to fix what's making you sick. He shares how this breakthrough could potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments for some of humanity's most challenging diseases.

recentItems.title: Why Great Art Requires Risk | Alex Van Halen, David Lee Roth and Robert Vargas | TED
recentItems.description:
Van Halen drummer and co-founder Alex Van Halen and lead singer David Lee Roth sit down with visual artist Robert Vargas, who paints freehand murals up to twenty stories tall, to reveal the two-step recipe behind great art: do your homework, then break every rule. Along the way, they swap stories about heartbreak, good luck charms — and why you should rehearse for what goes wrong. (Recorded at TEDxFargo on July 29, 2026)

recentItems.title: Want Someone to Change? Ask This Question | Philip Jameson | TED
recentItems.description:
Why is it so hard to get someone to change? Leadership expert Philip Jameson has spent years watching people pitch smart ideas at work, only to be met with colleagues resistant to adjusting how things get done. He breaks down why people push back against change — and the one question that could help your next idea take flight. (Recorded at TED@BCG on August 18, 2026)

recentItems.title: Why Clean Energy Is an Unstoppable Force | Michael Liebreich | TED
recentItems.description:
Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing? Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again. Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required. The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected. (Recorded at TED Countdown: The Next Ten on October 15, 2026)

recentItems.title: "Deep listening” can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and divides #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Do you avoid talking to people you disagree with? Author and mediator Emily Kasriel thinks you should try it out. She explains why engaging with ideas that bother you is one of the most powerful things you can do — and presents her framework for “deep listening” that can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and political divides.
